objects: Images represented as sequences of fixed-size image patches, with each patch converted into a vector representation and given positional information.
assumptions: Assumes far less image-specific inductive bias than CNNs — no built-in locality or translation-equivariance; spatial relationships between patches must be learned entirely from data rather than being architecturally assumed.
guarantees: The method empirically achieves strong image-classification performance and can outperform state-of-the-art convolutional networks while using substantially fewer computational resources to train when pretrained on large amounts of data.
formalism.operation: Split an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed each patch, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder.

evidence_spans.objects: We split an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed each of them, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder.
evidence_spans.assumptions: Vision Transformer has much less image-specific inductive bias than CNNs... all spatial relations between the patches have to be learned from scratch.
evidence_spans.guarantees: When pre-trained on large amounts of data and transferred to multiple mid-sized or small image recognition benchmarks (ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB, etc.), Vision Transformer (ViT) attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train.
